summary: This bill amends the Higher Education Act to require colleges to adopt and publicly report policies prohibiting student harassment based on race, sex, disability, religion, or similar traits (including via electronic messaging or campus networks) and to create a $50 million annual competitive grant program for prevention, counseling, and training programs at those institutions.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes $50 million annually for fiscal years 2026-2031 to fund a new competitive grant program for anti-harassment initiatives at higher education institutions. This represents new federal spending rather than any reduction or reallocation from existing programs.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare delivery, insurance, coverage models, or medical services.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration, visas, border policy, or immigrant protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion access, restrictions, or reproductive rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental regulations or climate policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net benefits.

The bill amends the Higher Education Act to impose new federal disclosure and policy requirements on institutions of higher education regarding harassment and creates a federal grant program administered by the Department of Education. This increases federal involvement and mandates in postsecondary education.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance policy.
The bill addresses institutional disciplinary procedures for harassment but does not alter criminal sentencing, policing practices, or broader criminal justice policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill authorizes new spending without any offsetting measures or debt-reduction mechanisms, but its primary focus is not fiscal policy.

The bill explicitly requires institutions to adopt policies prohibiting harassment based on sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, sex stereotypes, and sex characteristics (including intersex traits), and funds programs to prevent such harassment. This directly expands legal protections and institutional obligations for LGBTQ+ individuals.
The bill contains no provisions related to foreign aid.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access or election procedures.
The bill defines and addresses harassment conducted via electronic communications and messaging services but does not impose new privacy regulations or oversight on technology companies.
The bill contains no provisions related to unions, collective bargaining, or worker/employer relations.

The bill adds religion as a protected characteristic for harassment prohibitions and references existing civil rights statutes without creating new religious exemptions, thereby reinforcing anti-discrimination frameworks over potential religious carve-outs.
